comments.body: there are a couple too many line breaks here, where does the change come from?
@dsfaccini dropped them, lmk if lgty now
There doesn't seem to be a particular reason why this needs to add to an existing list, so I'd prefer to just have it return a list that we can then combine at the call site
Let's use the method here as well just for consistency.
Can we instead test `assert call_args == snapshot()` as we have below? When you run the test, the snapshot will be filled in automatically

I did that, except the problem with `BinaryContent` is that the `data` attr repr is extremely large and that would clutter the file.
I instead replaced it with the `image_content` fixture used in the test and `snapshot()` is happy with it

Now that we do the joining-if-all-strings at the end, I think this can be simplified as follows:

```suggestion
    content = content if isinstance(content, Sequence) else [content]
    
    sections.append(f'<{tag}>')
    for item in content:  # type: ignore[reportUnknownVariableType]
        if isinstance(item, str | MultiModalContent):
            sections.append(item)
        else:
            sections.append(_stringify(item))
    sections.append(f'</{tag}>')
```

@DouweM I can see your refactoring point, however as is, no your snippet will not produce the intended result bcs strings are instances of `Sequence` and therefore we would newline after each character. Then, with this out of the way (easily fixable), this means we change a little the list we produce. Specifically when at least one item in `sections` is not a str, then we return a list of all the items instead of concatenating the string parts. Example above, look at the **dummy rubric** part: it goes from one concatenated string to its parts. Can you confirm which format is best for the LLMJudge to receive, if any? Then I can proceed with the changes.

@Clement-Lelievre Ah good point on str being a sequence :) So yeah then we have to do `isinstance(str)` first.

The rubric being broken up into items is OK, the model will receive/interpret it identically.

ok done

(so in fact there's no strong reason to concatenate into a single str when all items are strs, but I left it as is as it doesn't harm)
